Tokenization is the process of converting raw text into a sequence of numeric identifiers that a language model can consume. Modern byte pair encoding schemes begin by treating every byte as its own token, then repeatedly merge the most frequent adjacent pair until the target vocabulary size is reached. The result is a tradeoff between vocabulary size and the average number of tokens required to represent common words, which directly affects both the memory footprint of the embedding layer and the cost of the model's attention computation.
